subject: Opaque hop causing burst latency and 5xx errors — Meridian Retail escalation
messages:
From: Alex Cho <acho@meridianretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@meridianretail.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency spikes and 5xxs for inference calls - urgent

Jordan —

We're seeing a sudden increase in inference latency and intermittent 5xx errors for our checkout recommendation calls that started ~07:45 PT this morning. P95 latency has jumped from ~150ms to 1.2s and error rate is now ~6%. This is impacting checkout throughput and causing failed sessions.

Attached is a small sample of the last 60mins of latency metrics and a couple of failing request IDs. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side or if it's something in our VPC peering? We need an ETA because procurement is asking about credits if this keeps happening.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Cho | Head of Platform Engineering | Meridian Retail
[Attachment: latency-metrics.csv]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cho <acho@meridianretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:28:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes and 5xxs for inference calls - urgent

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the data. We're looking immediately.

Quick notes:
- Can you share a traceroute / mtr from the affected app host to the Redwood ingress? That helps identify opaque hops.
- Are the failures concentrated in a specific region or availability zone?
- We'll start by checking VPC peering metrics, NAT gateway saturation, and our proxy chain (we've seen multi-proxy serialization amplify latency).

Marissa/Vivek — looping you in for network-level checks. If this is a peering/DNS flip, we need to treat it as an Exec-level SLA incident. Alex, I will follow up with a timeline within 30 minutes.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Alex Cho <acho@meridianretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:46:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes and 5xxs for inference calls - urgent

Alex/Jordan — initial triage summary: we've seen an increase in TCP retransmits and higher RTT across a subset of customer flows that traverse an older peering path through Provider-X in us-west-2. Traceroutes (attached) show an opaque hop at Provider-X that intermittently drops packets, which triggers our proxy chain to retry and serialize requests causing p95 amplification.

Preliminary actions taken (08:40 PT):
- Bounced the edge proxy pool in us-west-2 to clear stuck connections.
- De-prioritized the Provider-X path in our smart routing for Meridian's tenant (should reduce exposed sessions).
- Opened NET-2104 with infra to request route preference and to validate NAT conntrack.

Next steps: if Provider-X cannot stabilize, we recommend temporarily routing Meridian traffic via the backup peering path (adds ~40ms baseline but removes the intermittent 5xxs). Vivek, can you authorize the route shift? I drafted a short action plan PDF.

Attachments: traceroutes.txt, redwood-action-plan.pdf

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Cho <acho@meridianretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@meridianretail.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@meridianretail.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:03:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes and 5xxs for inference calls - urgent

Thanks for the quick analysis. Sylvia and Procurement are now on the thread — they're asking if Redwood can commit to a mitigation ETA and whether routing to the backup peering path is an approved operational change (we need confirmation this won't affect data residency or compliance).

If the backup path is acceptable I prefer a temporary route shift — lower p95 variance is better for checkout success than a slightly higher baseline. Also please confirm if this incident will be written up for the outage report and if credits will be considered given impact.

-Alex
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Cho <acho@meridianretail.com>
Cc: Sylvie Executive <ceo_ops@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:18:59 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes and 5xxs for inference calls - urgent

Team / Alex — I reviewed the action plan. Authorize temporary routing to the backup peering path for Meridian Retail effective immediately. Operational notes:
- Switch will be performed at 09:30 PT and is expected to take ~6 minutes to converge for tenant traffic.
- No data will leave the configured region; routing via backup peer respects routing controls.
- If the backup path shows sustained stability for 24h, we'll schedule a permanent rollover and follow-up RCA.

Jordan, please prepare an executive summary for Meridian's leadership and cc me. Marissa, push NET-2104 to high priority and include Provider-X contact traces. Also mark incident for credit review in billing queue.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | VP, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cho <acho@meridianretail.com>, Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@meridianretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@meridianretail.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes and 5xxs for inference calls - urgent

Sylvia / Alex — quick executive summary and status as of 15:43 PT:

What happened: an intermittent packet-loss/queuing behavior at a transit hop owned by Provider-X (opaque hop) started 2026-06-21 07:45 PT and caused amplified latency and 5xxs through our proxy chain for a subset of Meridian traffic.

What we did:
- Rebalanced tenant traffic away from Provider-X to backup peering at 09:30 PT on 2026-06-21.
- Bounced edge proxy pool and invalidated affected connections.
- Opened NET-2104 and engaged Provider-X; we're tracking contact and remediation.

Current status: p95 reduced to ~210ms; error rate back under 0.5%. No further spike since the route shift.

Next steps:
- Keep backup routing for 24 hours, then re-evaluate permanent rollover.
- Engineering RCA doc due EOD Wed; billing will review credit eligibility and reach out separately.
- We'll share a clean packet capture and the Provider-X correspondence in the incident folder.

Attachments: redwood-action-plan.pdf (mitigation steps), latency-metrics.csv (post-switch sample)

Appreciate your patience. Happy to hop on a quick call with Syliva and Alex if you'd like a live briefing.

Jordan Blake | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0183
[Attachment: redwood-action-plan.pdf]
